findings.name: P77_A-P77_E_OK
findings.message: P77_A exists in the repository but never emits this condition

fixes.title: Make the named producer emit it
fixes.label: P77_CHAIN/P77_A emits P77_A-P77_E_OK
fixes.explanation: Adds OUTCOND + P77_A-P77_E_OK to P77_CHAIN/P77_A, the job the condition name points to: the waiting job then runs after it.

fixes.title: Stop waiting for it
fixes.label: P77_CHAIN/P77_E stops waiting for P77_A-P77_E_OK
fixes.explanation: Removes INCOND P77_A-P77_E_OK (and its cleanup, OUTCOND -) from the waiting job: it no longer waits for a condition nobody emits.

fixes.title: Stop waiting for it
fixes.label: P77_CHAIN/P77_F stops waiting for WEIRD_NAME
fixes.explanation: Removes INCOND WEIRD_NAME (and its cleanup, OUTCOND -) from the waiting job: it no longer waits for a condition nobody emits.

findings.name: P77_F
findings.message: JOBNAME used by more than one job in the folder

fixes.title: Number the repeated JOBNAMEs
fixes.label: rename P77_CHAIN/P77_F~2 -> P77_F2
fixes.explanation: Gives the second and later jobs called P77_F in the folder a numeric suffix (P77_F2, P77_F3…); the JOBNAME changes in Control-M too.

findings.name: P77_B-P77_C_OK
findings.message: waited for but never deleted by the consumer (no OUTCOND SIGN="-")

fixes.title: Delete it after use
fixes.label: P77_CHAIN/P77_C deletes P77_B-P77_C_OK once it ran
fixes.explanation: Adds the cleanup OUTCOND - P77_B-P77_C_OK to P77_CHAIN/P77_C: the condition is removed after use, so it cannot release the next run by mistake.

findings.name: P77_OLDNAME-P77_D_OK
findings.message: name embeds P77_OLDNAME -> P77_D but the link is P77_C -> P77_D

fixes.title: Rename to the standard name
fixes.label: rename P77_OLDNAME-P77_D_OK -> P77_C-P77_D_OK
fixes.explanation: Renames the condition to <PRODUCER>-<CONSUMER>_OK from the jobs it really links, in every job that uses it.

findings.name: P77_A-P77_C_OK

fixes.title: Make the named consumer wait for it
fixes.label: P77_CHAIN/P77_C waits for P77_A-P77_C_OK
fixes.explanation: Adds INCOND P77_A-P77_C_OK to P77_CHAIN/P77_C, the job the condition name points to, and the cleanup (OUTCOND -): it then runs after P77_CHAIN/P77_A.

fixes.title: Stop emitting it
fixes.label: P77_CHAIN/P77_A stops emitting P77_A-P77_C_OK
fixes.explanation: Removes OUTCOND + P77_A-P77_C_OK from P77_CHAIN/P77_A: no job waits for it.

dangling.looks_for: A job waits for a condition that nobody emits, and the name of the condition names a job that is in the repository.
dangling.why: The job that waits never starts by itself: the job it names does not release it.
dangling.fix: Either the named job starts emitting the condition (one line added to that job), or the waiting job stops waiting for it.

dangling-unknown.looks_for: A job waits for a condition that nobody emits, and the name does not say who should.
dangling-unknown.why: The job that waits never starts by itself, and nothing here tells where the condition should come from.
dangling-unknown.fix: The waiting job stops waiting for it; when it comes from another application, leave it as it is.

dangling-external.looks_for: A job waits for a condition that nobody here emits, named after a job that is not in this repository.
dangling-external.why: Usually nothing is wrong: another application emits it. It is listed so that a mistyped name does not hide among them.
dangling-external.fix: None is needed when the other application exists; the waiting job can stop waiting for it otherwise.

unconsumed.looks_for: A job emits a condition that nobody waits for, though the name names a job that is in the repository, or nobody at all.
unconsumed.why: The link the name promises does not exist: the named job runs without waiting for this one.
unconsumed.fix: Either the named job starts waiting for the condition, or the emitting job stops emitting it.

unconsumed-external.looks_for: A job emits a condition that nobody here waits for, named after a job that is not in this repository.
unconsumed-external.why: Usually nothing is wrong: another application waits for it.
unconsumed-external.fix: None is needed when the other application exists; the job can stop emitting it otherwise.

stale-name.looks_for: The name of a condition names two jobs, and the condition links two others.
stale-name.why: It works, and it misleads whoever reads it: the name tells of a chain that is not the one that runs. A job renamed or a condition reused leaves it so.
stale-name.fix: The condition is renamed after the jobs it really links, in every job that uses it, other folders included.

non-standard-name.looks_for: The name of a condition is not made of the two jobs it links (PRODUCER-CONSUMER_OK or PRODUCER-TO-CONSUMER).
non-standard-name.why: Nothing fails. The names alone do not tell who releases whom.
non-standard-name.fix: The condition is renamed to the standard name, in every job that uses it.

never-cleaned.looks_for: A job waits for a condition and never deletes it once it ran.
never-cleaned.why: The condition stays in Control-M and can release the next run of the job before its predecessor ran again.
never-cleaned.fix: The waiting job gets one line that deletes the condition after use.

duplicate-jobname.looks_for: Two or more jobs of one folder have the same JOBNAME, and the repository was told not to number them.
duplicate-jobname.why: The name does not tell them apart: a condition named after it could be of either.
duplicate-jobname.fix: The second and later ones get a number at the end (NAME2, NAME3); the conditions that carry the name and belong to them follow.
